newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast crude rises on futures, but trade thin.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast crude rises on futures, but trade thin.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices edged up Tuesday, in line with higher domestic crude oil markets while local traders continued to stay out of the spot market, traders said.

Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, the region's benchmark grade, remained unsold for August on a spot basis, though Atlantic Richield Co. (ARCO) sold three cargoes on a formula basis to two Northwest refiners, traders said.
With the discount flat, outright prices for ANS crude oil were pulled up by slightly higher NYMEX and WTI cash prices.
Line 63 barrels also gained in line with the NYMEX and cash crude.
Kern River and Wilmington crudes -- California heavy grades -- were unchanged.
Foreign spot buying remained quiet, traders said.
Both U.S Oil and Tosco's Los Angeles and Bay refineries remained at reduced rates of crude oil runs, traders said, due to poor refining margins.
